title: Distribution range size is correlated with host-plant width but not with intraspecific wing colour diversity in winter geometrid moths
content:
Abstract
Recent studies have demonstrated that intraspecific colour variation promotes species-level ecological success, including range size expansion and long-term stability, in various taxa. However, how colour diversity in each sex independently contributes to species-level ecological properties has rarely been elucidated. In this study, we conducted interspecific comparisons to examine the distribution range size of winter geometrid moths in Japan, focusing on intraspecific colour variation in the male wings and larval dietary breadth of each species. Because females of winter geometrid moths are wingless or have reduced wings, we are able to evaluate the effects of colour diversity in males on species-level properties without any confounding effect of female colour diversity. We found no significant relationship between male wing colour diversity and the distribution range size, whereas the distribution range size increased significantly with larval dietary breadth. Our results suggest that in Japanese winter geometrid moths, in contrast to niche width, intraspecific colour diversity in males may not play a role in species-level range size.
